title: An ideal-power-torsion-free carrier of an open section
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $I$ ideal-sheaf data [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $E$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $U$ open with $V(I)=X\setminus U$. Write $P_n$ for the recursive powers with inclusion $j_n:P_n\to\mathcal O_X$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. For every $s\in E(U)$ there are a quasi-coherent module $G$, a monomorphism $g:G\to E$, and $t\in G(U)$ with $g_U(t)=s$, such that for every $n$, open $W$, and $x\in G(W)$, if $j_{n,V}(b)x|_V=0$ for every open $V\subseteq W$ and $b\in P_n(V)$, then $x=0$.

source.place: Tag 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open), first two paragraphs of the proof, through the construction of F prime.

proof.text: Extend the finite-type image of the section map O_U to E|U to a finite-type quasi-coherent submodule G of E. On the Noetherian scheme this submodule is coherent.

The quasi-coherent annihilators of I-powers form an increasing chain in G. By ACC they stabilize at T=G_r. Artin-Rees yields c with I^(r+c)G intersect T=0. The submodule G prime=I^(r+c)G has zero annihilator for every I-power and agrees with G on U.

Let G be the ideal-power product selected by Artin-Rees, with its inclusion into E. On U it agrees with the finite-type carrier H, so the section lifts. Any section of G killed by an ideal power belongs to the stabilized annihilator T of H. It is also in G, whose intersection with T is zero; injectivity of G into H then forces the section to vanish. This argument applies on every open and includes n=0.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_idealPower_torsionFree_section_carrier
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (E : X.Modules) [E.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.Opens)
    (hI : (I.support : Set X) = (U : Set X)ᶜ) (s : E.val.obj (op U)) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (g : G ⟶ E) (t : G.val.obj (op U)),
      G.IsQuasicoherent ∧ Mono g ∧ g.val.app (op U) t = s ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (W : X.Opens) (x : G.val.obj (op W)),
        (∀ (V : X.Opens) (h : V ≤ W)
          (b : (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).1.val.obj (op V)),
          ((idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2.val.app (op V) b : Γ(X, V)) •
            G.val.map (homOfLE h).op x = 0) → x = 0
